newsitem.title: UK: Labour's Brown not up to my job -UK's Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Labour's Brown not up to my job -UK's Clarke.

text.p: Chancellor Kenneth Clarke said on Monday he doubted Labour economic spokesman Gordon Brown was fit to take his place at the Treasury, and accused him of dealing in double-speak and sound bites.
"Even though I respect Gordon Brown, I frankly do not think he is up to the job of being Chancellor," Clarke said in an election campaign speech in St Albans, north of London.
"It's a tough job that requires experience and judgement. I've got the experience and I have made difficult judgements that have turned out right."
"By contrast, Mr Brown is part of a lightweight, superficial Labour team that parrots our slogans but has no idea of how to deliver the goods."

Trumpeting Conservative success in producing an extended period of low-inflation economic growth, Clarke added: "Labour want us to halt the long-run strategy we have for the revival of Britain. They want Britain to take a holiday from history."

Clarke said the Conservatives had "rumbled" Labour over the fact that there would be a hole in their financing plans if they did not proceed with planned privatisations, and the opposition party was now in full retreat.

"Why was there no mention of privatisation in the leaked first draft of their Business Manifesto 10 days ago? Why can they not commit to privatise London Underground? Why only six months ago were they describing NATS (National Air Traffic Services) privatisation as crazy'?" he asked.
Brown earlier on Monday refused to rule out going ahead with a sell-off of NATS.
Now, Clarke said, the Conservatives would put Labour under pressure over other aspects of their policy which would leave a "black hole" in the public finances.
"Mr Brown runs away from these questions. He seems to think that he can fool the British people with double-speak and sound bites," Clarke said.
"Labour will not come clean on the critical issues of taxing, spending and borrowing. They are not fit to govern." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 5528
